name: Rainmaker SPV

terms.sponsorMoicNote: From Braiden’s GC underwrite scorecard (90/100), which is the first source to produce a base case at all — the company itself publishes no target multiple. Scenario grid, NET to the LP after dilution and SPV economics: downside 1.2-3.0x over 6-8 years, BASE 5.5-13.0x over 7-10 years, upside 16.0-30.0x+ over 10+ years. Gross entry-to-exit is higher: 1.7-4.4x, 8.9-20.0x and 26.7-44.4x+. The file carries 5.5x — the LOW end of the base net range — because the model puts this figure in the winner branch, and using the midpoint there would flatter it.
terms.holdNote: The underwrite puts the base case at 7-10 years, downside 6-8 and upside 10+. Modelled at 8. IPO was described as not viable until well past unicorn status; secondary sale is the more likely early liquidity route.
terms.minimumNote: $10,000 minimum into the SPV; up to $6M of allocation was offered to GC.
terms.feeNote: Accessed through a Spacestation-sponsored AngelList SPV, NOT the main fund. Fees are FRONT-LOADED at roughly 8-10% in year one, described as economically similar to 2-and-20 over the life. That drag comes off the top of whatever the company does.
terms.instrumentNote: A SAFE at a $450M cap against a Series B2 that closed at $350M post. The expected 20% discount is the important term: it protects if the next priced round comes in below $450M, functioning much like a full-ratchet anti-dilution provision, which is rare. Information rights expected; pro-rata and major-investor status pushed for; MFN thought unlikely.
terms.qsbsNote: Does NOT qualify for QSBS — the company exceeds the gross-assets threshold.

scenarioGrid.basis: Net to the LP after dilution and SPV economics; gross figures in brackets.
scenarioGrid.note: The base case requires moving beyond legacy service contracts into larger state, federal, international and corporate contracts. The upside requires verified water sales to become a real market rather than a narrative.

revenue.note: This resolves the disagreement between the two June calls. One reported "$14M in 2024", which was a year out — $14.7M is 2025. The other gave ~$15M 2025 and $42.6M 2026E, which matches to rounding. Contribution margin 39% (2024) expanding to a projected 50% (2026). EBITDA break-even projected 2027, which would make the company default-alive post-close if execution tracks.

terms.raised: ~$110M across four priced rounds plus SAFE activity in roughly 30 months, including a ~$40M Series B2 at a $350M post-money.

structure: Rainmaker Technology Corporation, a cloud-seeding and water-production company, held through a Spacestation-sponsored SPV on a SAFE. The return is pure venture multiple expansion — no yield, no preference, no downside protection. The bull case rests on the company being classified as sovereign infrastructure ("American Dynamism", ~28x revenue comps) rather than as a drone company (~5x) or water infrastructure (~3x); entry at ~10x forward revenue is cheap against the first frame and two to three times overpriced against the others.
_about: Global deal facts only. Terms are identical for everyone who bought the same deal, so they live here rather than being retyped by each holder. Nothing personal is in this file: your commitment, funding dates, thesis and notes stay in your own tracker and never leave your machine.
source: GC underwrite scorecard by Braiden Shaw (90/100, with the hyper-realistic exit-scenario grid); Spacestation underwriting call and founder Q&A, SLC, 13 and 16 June 2026 (Granola); the GC deal-comparison IC memo; Rainmaker pitch deck and deal memo (image-only).
liquidityNote: One company, so it exits on one date rather than selling down. Spacestation controls any SPV-level secondary decision on behalf of all LPs, so the timing is not the holder’s to choose.
keyRisks: Valuation. $450M is not cheap on current revenue, and the Series B2 closed at $350M weeks earlier. It only works if government, federal, international and corporate demand keeps converting into contracted revenue.

Comp frame. Dual-use / American Dynamism comps trade at 15x-46x revenue with a cohort median around 28x; entry is framed at ~10.8x forward / 30.6x LTM. If the market decides this is a drone or water-services company instead, the entry is two to three times overpriced.
Political and perception risk. One high-profile weather event, even unrelated, can trigger legislation and media cycles. People confuse cloud seeding with geoengineering.
Peer-reviewed publication is targeted for late 2026 and is not yet done, so part of the validation remains company-driven.
Hard operating business: government sales, field deployment, hardware reliability and international logistics all have to work together.
Key-person risk around the founder, partially offset by an unusually deep bench.
Side-letter terms not final. Without pro-rata and major-investor rights there is exposure but less control over follow-on ownership.

reportedFigures.note: Operating figures as reported on the June 2026 calls. The two sessions did not agree with each other, which is recorded rather than reconciled.
reportedFigures.revenue: One session gave $0 (2023), $14M (2024), $41M (2025) with $100M+ projected in year three; another gave ~$15M (2025) and a $42.6M 2026 target.
reportedFigures.margin: Contribution margin ~42%, with an automation target near 80%. ~$1M contract minimum.
reportedFigures.balance: Post-close cash $80M+, burn $2-3M/month, roughly 30 months of runway.

provisionalNote: To be precise about what is and is not settled, because most of this card is solid. CONFIRMED by two independent sources (the GC underwrite scorecard and the June 2026 underwriting call): the $450M post-money cap, the ~28% premium to the $350M Series B, the $10,000 minimum, the SPV’s 8-10% front-loaded fees, no QSBS, and the scenario grid. NOT CONFIRMED, because no executed SAFE or side letter has been read: whether the cap is cap-only or cap plus discount, whether the SAFE is pre- or post-money, the scope of any MFN, and what a holder receives if the company is acquired before conversion. Those are side-letter mechanics, not economics — they change how many shares the money converts into, not whether the thesis holds. One more thing worth keeping in view: the scenario grid is the GC UNDERWRITER’S analysis, not the company’s own projection. Rainmaker publishes no target multiple at all. Send the executed SAFE and this flag comes off.

underwrite.source: GC underwrite scorecard by Braiden Shaw

keyFacts: Acquired NAWC, a 75-year-old legacy cloud-seeding operator, bringing contracts, NOAA reporting standing and 200 ground-based silver-iodide generators across four Western states.

Built the full stack in-house: custom electric drones (Elijah, 15,000-foot ceiling, icing tested), a phased-array radar (Eden) and a software layer (Stratus) that improves targeting and attribution with every mission.
First commercial operator to produce radar and satellite-confirmed attribution of man-made snowfall in real storm conditions; 80+ such events in a single winter season.
Holds a broad FAA waiver for autonomous drone flight in clouds and icing, day or night, across the continental U.S.
Economics of the category: cloud seeding at $5-15 per acre-foot against desalination at $2,000-3,400 per acre-foot.
Positioned in the highest-urgency geography: Colorado River Basin, Great Salt Lake watershed, Utah, Idaho, Wyoming, Colorado.
Of 31 proposed state cloud-seeding bans, 28 were dropped, and several states later moved toward funding programmes for the first time.
Cap table includes Lowercarbon (led the Series A and anchors the current round), 1517, Long Journey, Day One, Tamarack Global, Starship, Sovereign’s Capital and DCVC.
Team of ~120 under Augustus Doricko, with hires from Lockheed Martin supply chain, NOAA hurricane research, Anduril/REGENT and Navy aviation.
